workItems.rationale: Major migration against a new, fast-moving server protocol. The provider construction and mapper are rewritten rather than patched, and uncertainty remains in the `question` deny and 2.x event shapes. Rescored 11 → 5 only because the former 11-point row (an invalid point value) was split into W1, W7, and W8, which together held 11 at v1.2. The v1.4 W7 re-estimate raises the combined W1 + W7 + W8 effort to 13 without changing W1. W1 keeps the original pre-review core of construction, lifecycle, auth, version gate, permissions, and mapper. The turn loop and R3/R4 work moved to W7; the factory seam, live test, and R6 work moved to W8. Architecture stays neutral: process management moves from the SDK into 5x (+), offset by removing the 1.x SDK startup path (−).

workItems.title: Provider turn loop: prompt admission and streamed completion, server-evidence polling fallback settling through a shared `settleTurn`, compaction-safe durable-transcript text recovery (`readTurnText` with paginated `session.message.list`), `run()` over `runStreamed()`, and their unit tests
workItems.rationale: Split from the former 11-point W1 row with no change to scope. Rescored 3 → 5 in v1.4 as a re-estimate of the same scope, not a scope change. Two things were missing from the 3. First, the v1.2 split held W1 + W7 + W8 at 11 by arithmetic, which left the core turn loop about one point once the R3 and R4 increments were counted. Second, the R3 closure correction (addendum iteration 2, reviewer effortDelta +1: newly settled `failed`/`interrupted` outcomes reach `settleTurn` without an assistant-message prerequisite, plus SSE-drop-before-assistant fixtures) was carried only as run_a9914ec93486's final-corrections allowance and never entered this ledger. A new run inherits no correction allowance, so the row must carry it. Combined work: the core turn loop (subscription handshake, prompt admission, streamed mapping, inactivity timeout and interrupt, `run()` over `runStreamed()` with the summary turn), replacing about 540 lines (`opencode.ts:186–727`); R3 server-evidence polling and shared `settleTurn` (+1), and its closure correction (+1); R4 paginated durable text recovery (+1). About 25 scripted cases in the rewritten 1,126-line `opencode.test.ts` cover this work. That re-estimates above 3. 4 is not an allowed value, so the row is scored 5 rather than rounded down to 3. Uncertainty sits in stream timing and interrupt behavior. Includes R3 (+1 reviewer effortDelta: polling completes on server-side evidence and settles through the streamed path's terminal handler, with outcome, stale-state, clock-skew, timeout, and cancel cases; closure +1 as above) and R4 (+1: a paginated `session.message.list` fallback when compaction drops the prompt from context, with an explicit missing-boundary error). Architecture neutral: one turn loop replaces the duplicated 1.x run paths and recovery polling, and the corrections reuse it rather than adding an abstraction.

workItems.title: Factory verification and live evidence: external-provider verification and close-on-failure in `src/providers/factory.ts`, the `OpenCodeFactoryDeps` test seam with fake healthy, unauthorized, and cleanup tests, network-free bundled plugin-loading case, and the opt-in live test covering managed and authenticated external mode against a test-owned server
workItems.rationale: Split from the former 11-point W1 row with no change to scope. Re-examined in v1.4 and unchanged; the combined W1 + W7 + W8 effort is 13 after the W7 re-estimate. Includes R6 (+1 reviewer effortDelta): an injectable factory seam with fake verification and cleanup tests, plus a live authenticated external-mode run against a test-owned server that survives `close()`. Architecture neutral: the seam is a test-only dependency parameter on the existing factory, and the live test extends the existing opt-in fixture.

workItems.title: Prompted structured output: `structured-output.ts` string-aware top-level extractor, schema-wrapped summary prompt, corrective retries
workItems.rationale: A small new module inside the provider subsystem replaces a server feature 2.x removed. +1 architecture because 5x now owns extraction and retry policy for OpenCode, beside the Cursor package's separate extractor. Rescored 2 → 3 for R5: the extractor is a new forward scanner with string, escape, and depth state and nested, escaped-quote, string-brace, multiple-object, and array rejection tests. It does not port the Cursor package's backward brace counter. Architecture unchanged: the scanner sits inside the already planned module.

workItems.title: Delete dead TUI controller, permissions, detect, and event-router modules, their tests, and the stale init hint

debtClaim.before: `src/tui/controller.ts`, `src/tui/permissions.ts`, `src/tui/detect.ts`, and `src/utils/event-router.ts` import `@opencode-ai/sdk/v2` types, are imported by nothing in `src/` or `packages/`, and implement `opencode attach` / `--tui-listen` behavior that no command exposes; `test/unit/tui/*` exercises them.
debtClaim.after: The four modules and `test/unit/tui/*` are deleted, `init` no longer prints the `--tui-listen` hint, and dropping the 1.x SDK requires no port of attach or permission-reply logic to 2.x.

workItems.rationale: Deletion only, after confirming there are no importers. Removes about 1.2k production lines and about 1.4k test lines tied to the retired `opencode attach` path. R1: moved to Phase 1, ahead of the provider port, so the SDK dependency removal and its typecheck gate in Phase 2 can pass. Reordering existing work leaves effort and architecture unchanged. v1.4 evidence: completed in Phase 1 (`fa19978d`, independently reviewed in `ce74d860`). Actual work matched the score: about 1.23k production lines and 1.37k test lines deleted, plus two one-line edits. Score unchanged.

workItems.title: `5x doctor` OpenCode version check and `opencode.url` config description
workItems.rationale: A new detect-only check in the existing doctor registry, plus a config description update. +1 for one more check to maintain.

workItems.title: Harness assets: 2.x agent frontmatter, `NATIVE_DELEGATE_TOOL` / `NATIVE_AGENT_PARAM` tokens and OpenCode `sessionID` continuation, OpenCode background launch/await/continue lifecycle tokens, base skill and orchestrator wording and continuation references, asset-impact verification across delegation modes and install/sync paths, live installed native delegation and continuation exercise
workItems.rationale: Crosses harness templates, the token system, five base skills, and the install/sync path. Rescored 3 → 5 for R2 (the reviewer's effortDelta of 2). The work adds lifecycle tokens at every native launch and continuation-capture site, reworks the orchestrator's `task_id` continuation instructions, adds launch-versus-completion and continuation assertions in all four delegation modes, and adds one real delegation and continuation by the installed orchestrator on a live 2.x server. No new abstraction: the token mechanism already exists and gains entries, and Cursor output stays byte-identical.

findings.title: Tie settlement to delivery of the submitted prompt
findings.failure: A resumed invocation can settle against the previous execution, return the wrong reply or usage, or send a summary prematurely.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Require delivery evidence for the exact inbox item before settling either path; reject an active or overlapping session when ownership cannot be established. Add a same-session prior-terminal-before-delivery regression.

findings.title: Cancel pending work as well as running work
findings.failure: A cancelled external invocation can execute later, or interrupt a different execution.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Short-circuit a pre-aborted turn, assign a stable prompt ID before admission, and bound the RPCs. Cancel the owned pending item or interrupt the owned active execution, handling a delivery race. Add delayed-acknowledgment and queued-cancellation fixtures.

findings.title: Route headless forms by their actual session discriminator
findings.failure: The headless fallback ignores its own pending form and the invocation stalls.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Extract the nested form session and ID, test own and foreign forms, and explicitly exercise question denial or the fallback in the live test.

findings.title: Use an executable Phase 1 unit-test gate
findings.failure: The literal required Phase 1 command cannot provide passing evidence on the reviewed tree.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Spell the previously passing configured unit command in the gate: bun test --concurrent --parallel=2 --dots --timeout 15000 test/unit.

findings.title: Pipe managed stderr explicitly
findings.failure: Early startup errors lose the required stderr tail and child diagnostics bypass managed capture.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Specify piped stdout and stderr in the managed spawn options and assert both in the existing spawn-seam test.

findings.title: Exercise real reviewer output through 5x invoke
findings.failure: Both modes can pass the acceptance suite even if neither returns a CLI-validated reviewer verdict.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Seed a valid temp plan/run and run one unrecorded reviewer invoke in each existing mode fixture, checking role-specific ReviewerVerdict validation alongside the author checks.

findings.title: Require positive live evidence for the advertised minimum
findings.failure: The release can claim compatibility with an unverified minimum or pass the opt-in gate without exercising either mode.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Fail bad prerequisites when opted in, require both cases on the advertised minimum or raise it to the oldest verified release, and align the old-2.x error with that minimum and the doctor upgrade hint.

findings.title: Tie settlement to delivery of the submitted prompt
findings.failure: A valid delivered turn can be misreported as cancelled, or a resumed invocation can attribute another execution’s usage to its result.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Do not infer cancellation from separate negative reads; recheck delivery on an inbox miss. Use usage scoped to the owned reply window or fail closed when it cannot be attributed, and add regressions for both races.

findings.title: Cancel pending work as well as running work
findings.failure: A cancelled prompt can enqueue after cleanup declares it removed, or cleanup can interrupt another client’s replacement execution.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Reconcile uncertain admission within the cleanup bound and report uncertainty without claiming removal; do not resend after cancellation. Use session-wide interrupt only with separately established exclusivity. Add late-enqueue and replacement-execution regressions.

findings.title: Require positive live evidence for the advertised minimum
findings.failure: The implementation can copy an unverified minimum from the Phase 2 contract or reject the passing required-version evidence as inconsistent.
findings.lowestCostCorrection: Align the literal in Phase 2.2 with the 2.4.2 starting value and retain the positive live gate at the actual advertised minimum.
